title: Dewey Jackson, the loudest trumpeter on the river
summary: Dewey Jackson's volume on the boats and the fact that the band played jazz.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Working the Streckfus riverboats with Fate Marable

blocks.x: Now, Dewey Jackson’s band – what did Dewey Jackson play?
Dewey Jackson was a trumpet player himself. Loud trumpet player. And they used to say that he was the loudest player – cat that ever came down the Mississippi

River. They used to – sometimes the parents – the families would take their kids to the wharf and put them on the boat and then they would go back and party at home or something. The way that they would know that it was time to go pick up their kids – they could hear Dewey Jackson about ten miles up the river. [Terry makes a piercing wa-wa sound.] Loud. They say, “We’ve got to cut out. We’ve got to go pick up the kids.”
